label: Late in episodes, GO value rises when S2 is believed good or a2 was last chosen; D2 tracks S1 belief.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.square(ep_dec) ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * np.square(ep_dec) ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * np.square(ep_dec)
terms: (phase == GO) * belief_lo * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D1) * in_rew * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D2) * (state == S1) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_state == S1) * ep_dec**2 ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * ep_dec**2
explanation: Timing dominates this unit (R^2 0.90): it sits near -1 and ramps up strongly late in the episode, and every residual effect grows with episode time, so all terms are scaled by ep_dec^2. Beyond timing, at GO it is higher when the ideal observer believes S2 is good (negative belief_lo) and after an a2 choice; at D2 the sign flips, so it is higher when S1 is believed good (and when S1 is reached). At D1 the effects are small: slightly higher after a rewarded trial and after reaching S1. The free fit adds the D1 reward, D2 reached-state, GO previous-unrewarded and D1 terms (dev 0.33 against 0.26 for the short form). Large residuals vary from episode to episode late in the episode and none of the observed cues capture them. No future variables are used.
